triceratops-horridus.compositionDescription: High-oblique portrait depth split with a large lower foreground Triceratops, a small upper-bank Edmontosaurus, and a broad channel as negative space.
triceratops-horridus.prompt:
Create a NEW original portrait-oriented 4:5 naturalistic museum paleoart illustration for a dinosaur atlas for ages 5-14. Use the two attached project-owned generated images only as taxon identity references: the FIRST is Triceratops horridus and the SECOND is Edmontosaurus annectens. Do not copy their backgrounds or compositions.

Scene: latest Cretaceous, lower Hell Creek Formation floodplain after a light rain. A shallow meandering channel and open point bar divide exactly TWO animals. Place one adult Triceratops horridus as the large lower-left foreground focal animal, in calm three-quarter side view. Place one adult Edmontosaurus annectens in the upper-right midground beyond the water, clearly smaller only because of distance. Both animals are quietly aware of the landscape, not of each other. This is a cautious formation-fauna coexistence reconstruction, not a herd, partnership, chase, attack, or documented meeting.

Strict composition: vertical 4:5 frame, strong lower-left to upper-right diagonal, exactly two dinosaurs total, both complete from snout to tail tip, 8-10 percent clear margin around every body, every limb and foot readable, open water and empty ground separating the silhouettes, absolutely no overlap or contact.

Triceratops horridus identity lock: two long brow horns plus exactly one much shorter nasal horn; closed hooked beak; solid skull-attached frill with no holes; adult frill margin low and flattened, not a bead crown or spike crown; low long dinosaur body, exactly two forelimbs and two hind limbs, separated non-hoof feet, one complete tail. Avoid rhinoceros or elephant anatomy.

Edmontosaurus annectens identity lock: long low crestless skull, broad closed toothless duck bill, absolutely no tubular or bony head crest; deep hadrosaur body; low continuous soft midline ridge from neck along trunk, not a hump or sail; tiny restrained single row of tail spikes only behind the hips; exactly two mitten-like weight-bearing forehands, two hind limbs with broad three-hoof rear feet, and one complete stiff tail.

Environment: conifers, ferns, horsetails, low flowering shrubs, wet silt and shallow water; no modern lawn grass. Cool slate, teal, muted rust and ochre palette; overcast light breaking through mist; readable child-friendly silhouettes. No dramatic combat, no running, no roaring, no wounds, no blood, no carcass, no extra animals, no extra or fused limbs, no duplicated feet, no cropped tails, no text, no labels, no logo, no watermark. Do not imitate any named artist.

Edit the FIRST attached portrait paleoart candidate, preserving its exact vertical composition, river, lighting, landscape, foreground Triceratops horridus, color palette, full-body framing, and exactly-two-animal count. Use the SECOND attached image only as an anatomy reference for Edmontosaurus annectens.

Correct ONLY the distant upper-right Edmontosaurus limb readability. It must visibly have exactly TWO separate forelimbs ending in TWO separate compact mitten-like weight-bearing forehands, plus exactly TWO separate hind limbs ending in TWO separate broad three-hoof hind feet. Offset the far-side forelimb slightly so it is clearly visible behind the near-side forelimb without merging, duplicating, or adding a fifth limb. Keep its long low crestless skull, broad closed duck bill, low continuous soft neck-and-trunk midline ridge, tiny restrained tail-spike row only behind the hips, and one complete stiff tail. Keep the Edmontosaurus entirely on the far bank and fully separated from the Triceratops by open water. Do not change the Triceratops.

Exactly two dinosaurs total. No overlap, contact, chase, attack, blood, injury, carcass, extra limbs, fused legs, duplicated feet, cropped tail, text, label, logo, watermark, or named-artist imitation. Naturalistic museum paleoart for ages 5-14.

parasaurolophus-walkeri.compositionDescription: Low forest camera with an S-shaped trail, a horizontal fallen log, a large mid-left Parasaurolophus, and an upper-right Centrosaurus on a separate terrace.
parasaurolophus-walkeri.prompt:
Create a NEW original portrait-oriented 4:5 naturalistic museum paleoart illustration for a dinosaur atlas for ages 5-14. Use the two attached project-owned generated images only as taxon identity references: the FIRST is Parasaurolophus walkeri and the SECOND is Centrosaurus apertus. Do not copy their backgrounds or compositions.

Create a composition deliberately different from an opposite-river-bank diagonal scene. Scene: Late Cretaceous lower Dinosaur Park Formation, Alberta, in an open fern woodland on a raised levee after morning fog. No river or broad water channel; only damp soil, leaf litter, a few tiny puddles, ferns, horsetails, low flowering shrubs and conifers.

Composition: low ground-level camera with a tall forest canopy, an S-shaped dry trail, and a layered Z-depth arrangement. Put one adult Parasaurolophus walkeri as the large mid-left foreground focal animal in a clean LEFT-TO-RIGHT lateral three-quarter view, calmly reaching toward a low shrub. Keep the neck only gently lowered so the full head and crest remain separate from the body. Stagger all four limbs so exactly two short forelimbs with two separate compact rounded mitten-like forehands and exactly two hind limbs with two separate three-main-toe feet are clearly visible. Show the complete tail tip with 8-10 percent empty margin.

Put one adult Centrosaurus apertus in the upper-right midground on a slightly raised sunlit fern terrace, facing LEFT in a clean opposite-direction side three-quarter view. It is independently pausing, not looking at the Parasaurolophus. Stagger its exactly two forelimbs and two hind limbs so all four non-hoof feet are visible. Show its complete tail tip with empty margin. A low fallen conifer log and broad empty fern strip separate the depth layers, but NO tree, log, fern, body part, or shadow may cover either dinosaur's head, any limb, any foot, or any tail tip.

Exactly TWO dinosaurs total. Both full bodies are readable and spatially separated with no overlap or contact. Use the S-shaped trail, horizontal log, vertical tree trunks at the far frame edges, and alternating warm amber sun patches with cool fog to create a layered forest rhythm—not the previous high-oblique water split or straight lower-right-to-upper-left diagonal.

Parasaurolophus walkeri identity lock: broad closed toothless duck bill; one thick low tubular crest attached continuously to the skull, longer than the head and sweeping gently backward and slightly downward; thick neck; deep low hadrosaur body; exactly two short forelimbs with compact soft-tissue-bound mitten forehands, two strong hind limbs with three main toes, and one complete stiff tail held above ground. No teeth, no frill, no high hook, no extra crest, no skin sail.

Centrosaurus apertus adult identity lock: exactly one large nasal horn curving forward; only short low brow bosses, never long Triceratops brow horns; short solid skin-covered frill with no holes; paired central P1 hooks curving forward/down and smaller outer paired P2 hooks curving inward; low remaining ornament, never a Styracosaurus spike fan; exactly four limbs, four separated non-hoof feet, and one complete tail. Avoid rhinoceros anatomy.

Warm moss green, charcoal, muted russet and ochre palette, readable child-friendly silhouettes. No herd, family, partnership, migration claim, combat, running, roaring, wounds, blood, carcass, extra animals, extra or fused limbs, duplicated feet, cropped tails, text, labels, logo, watermark, or named-artist imitation.
